Ten awesome things about being Christian in the United States

this is all true, unfortunately. However most people seem to miss the connection between Christianity and America. Christianity has been forever engrained in the DNA of America. Yes the constitution and the Treaty of Tripoli say on paper that America is not a Christian nation. However the reality of the early American Republic would decisively state otherwise. Many of the states after the ratification of the constitution retained religious tests for public office long after. Massachusetts (the birthplace of the revolution!) did not get rid of religious tests until 1833. Pennsylvania, in their state constitution wrote that religious tests were mandatory. Christianity is likely the reason why the seeds of both female suffrage and prohibition were sewn in America's subconscious during the Second Great Awakening (revival of christian enthusiasm and growth of new christian sects such as Mormonism) between the 1830s and 1840s.1. Hell there is even a strong correlation with the First Great Awakening of the mid 1700s and the American Revolution (Though esteemed historians like that darn bastard Jon Butler, who managed to successfully throw the consensus of the relationship between Christian revivals and the American Revolution into absolute Chaos). There is a great book by Frank Lambert titled The Founding Fathers and the Place of Religion in America, which i will give a full bibliography down below that goes in depth with the relationship between Christianity and the formation of the American Union. If anyone is interested in learning more about religion in the early American republic, i would highly suggest you read it.

Despite this history, America has a long way before its government is truly secular, despite what polls may say about Americans becoming more secular, it will take many generations before nonreligious folk become more plentiful than religious folk because of how deeply engrained Christianity is in America's subconscious.
